implementation_steps_or_phases.name: Define relationship between mission requirements and use cases
implementation_steps_or_phases.completion_or_handoff: Each use case refines corresponding mission requirement(s).
implementation_steps_or_phases.evidence: Figure 1 shows requirements refined by Collect/Distribute Mission Data use cases.

implementation_steps_or_phases.name: Capture identified use cases
prerequisites: system boundary defined as CubeSat Enterprise

implementation_steps_or_phases.completion_or_handoff: Description identifies name, scope, actors/stakeholders, preconditions, trigger, and postconditions.

mapping_to_systems_engineering_activitie.lifecycle_gates: SRR/PDR/CDR or other gates are not mapped explicitly.
mapping_to_systems_engineering_activitie.evidence: Abstract says the method incorporates 'standard systems engineering practices such as: a top-down approach, requirements analysis, use case development, and functional analysis.'

implementation_pathway_tailoring.tailoring_notes: Tailored conceptually to university CubeSat teams and high-failure small-satellite missions; no quantitative cost/schedule tailoring evidence.
implementation_pathway_tailoring.adoption_guidance_rationale: Numbered method and examples are usable, but roles, templates/checklists, governance, reviews, and completion criteria are mostly implied.

toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.toolchain_architecture: Single SysML system model, illustrated in MagicDraw, containing requirements, use cases, use-case documentation, activities, refine links, and activity hierarchy/diagrams.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.data_flow_between_tools: not reported; all explicit artifact relationships are inside the SysML model/MagicDraw example.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_continuity: Requirements, use cases, and activities maintain semantic continuity through SysML refine relationships and common model elements. Continuity to downstream engineering tools is not reported.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.software_hardware_system_integration_rea: The model can decompose behaviors to space/ground segment and potentially subsystem levels, but no hardware/software integration readiness evidence, flat-sat/testbed link, or generated implementation artifacts are reported.

availability_reproducibility.reproducibility_notes: Figures and method steps support conceptual replication; no model file or package is provided.

evidence_quotes: SysML section: 'SysML is commonly used in MBSE... a graphical modeling language developed by the Object Management Group (OMG)'.
Step 5: 'In this example, the MagicDraw modeling tool developed by No Magic Inc. is used.'
Step 5: 'An alternative method would have been to create a hyperlink to a text file that contained the use case description.'

eps_elements_modeled.rationale: No solar panels, batteries, power conditioning/distribution, loads, margins, power budgets, degradation, fault protection, or EPS interfaces are modeled.

eps_requirements_represented.rationale: Only generic mission data collection/distribution requirements are represented.

verification_validation_artifacts.rationale: Verification of functional requirements is future work; no verification matrix/test procedure/check is integrated.

pre_physical_development_verification_me.rationale: No requirements-in-the-loop, simulation-in-the-loop, parametric checks, model checking, trade-study verification, or virtual integration mechanism is presented.

eps_verification_specific.evidence_model_integrated_vs_documented_: No EPS/system verification artifacts are present; use-case descriptions are captured in model documentation, but not verification artifacts.

integration_test_readiness.rationale: No hardware/software integration, flat-sat/testbed, environmental test, or operational validation linkage is reported.

evidence_quotes: Future Work: 'Related topics are... verification of the functional requirements.'
Table 1 requirements are Collect Mission Data and Distribute Mission Data, not EPS/power requirements.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text_or_paraphrase: Compared with a traditional document-based approach, MBSE/model-centric development can enhance communications, reduce development risk, improve quality, and enhance knowledge transfer; the system model serves as a single source of truth.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.mechanism_detail: A coherent system model captures requirements, design, analysis, and verification information; documentation is secondary/generated from the model.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect: Qualitative benefit asserted; no measured effect size.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.quote_location: Abstract and Section 2, Model-Based Systems Engineering
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.evidence_quote: Abstract: 'Some of the benefits of using an MBSE approach over a traditional document-based approach are: enhanced communications, reduced development risk, improved quality, and enhanced knowledge transfer [1].' Section 2: 'the model serves as a single-source-of-truth for the development team'.
threats_alternative_explanations: The benefits are imported from a general MBSE reference and not evaluated for this CubeSat method.
No CubeSat-specific baseline, metric, or stakeholder validation is reported.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text_or_paraphrase: The eight-step approach provides a repeatable, generalized method for CubeSat development teams and complements the INCOSE SSWG CubeSat Reference Model.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.mechanism_detail: Use mission requirements to identify and refine use cases, then model scenarios as activity hierarchies that can become reusable CubeSat reference-model content.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.linked_artifact_or_process: eight-step workflow; CubeSat Reference Model examples; requirements/use-case/activity model elements
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect: Qualitative: method is presented as repeatable/generalized; no reuse count or replication across missions is reported.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.evidence_quote: Abstract: 'This approach provides a repeatable, generalized method for CubeSat development teams to follow...' Introduction: the approach 'draws from existing methodologies to provide a repeatable, generalized method for university teams'.
threats_alternative_explanations: Examples are illustrative and limited to mission data collection/distribution.
No evidence that independent teams reused the method or reference model successfully.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text_or_paraphrase: The approach creates clear traceability from mission requirements to required functionality.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.mechanism_detail: SysML refine relationships connect mission requirements to use cases and connect use cases to activities.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.linked_artifact_or_process: Figure 1 requirements diagram; Figure 9 use case diagram with activity refine links; activity hierarchy
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect: Qualitative: visible refine links demonstrate a trace path in the example model; no trace coverage metric reported.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.evidence_quote: Conclusion: 'Traceability: There is clear traceability from the mission requirements to the functionality required to satisfy those requirements.' Step 7: 'This approach uses the refine relationship... for relating the activities to use cases.'
threats_alternative_explanations: Traceability is shown for two example mission requirements/use cases, not a full mission requirements set.
No verification of completeness or trace correctness by stakeholders/tools is reported.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text_or_paraphrase: Recursive activity decomposition can be applied at all mission hierarchy levels, producing a functional architecture/activity hierarchy that satisfies mission requirements.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.mechanism_detail: Top-level activities matching use cases are decomposed into actions and lower-level activities until the appropriate system hierarchy level is reached.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.linked_artifact_or_process: activity diagrams and BDD activity hierarchy for Collect Mission Data, including Figure 14
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect: Qualitative: example hierarchy decomposes Collect Mission Data through multiple sub-activities; no completeness metric or full-mission demonstration.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.evidence_quote: Step 8: 'The decomposition of activities into actions can continue down to the subsystem-level of the CubeSat. The end result can be shown in an activity hierarchy representing the full functional decomposition and the resulting functional architecture.' Conclusion: 'Recursive: The approach can be recursively applied at all levels of the mission hierarchy...'
threats_alternative_explanations: Only selected branches of the activity hierarchy are illustrated.
Future work is needed for allocation, interfaces, and verification, so full architecture completeness is not established.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text_or_paraphrase: The approach is general enough to be incorporated into many systems-engineering methodologies and is not dependent on a specific tool.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.mechanism_detail: The approach draws from common use-case and functional-analysis practices and represents artifacts in standard SysML.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect: Qualitative generalizability assertion; no cross-tool or cross-method implementation evidence.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.evidence_quote: Conclusion: 'Generalizability. This approach is not dependent on any specific tool and is general enough to be easily incorporated into many systems engineering methodologies.' Introduction: 'This approach does not attempt to develop an entirely new methodology. Instead, it draws from existing methodologies...'
threats_alternative_explanations: Only MagicDraw is shown in the paper.
No interoperability or implementation evidence for other tools/methodologies is provided.

model_governance_strategy.details: The system model is called a single-source-of-truth, but ownership, configuration/change control, review process, model-quality criteria, naming/versioning conventions, and repository governance are not reported.

traceability_to_project_deliverables_or_.details: Traceability from mission requirements to use cases and activities is shown; traceability to project deliverables, design reviews, assurance cases, or management reports is not shown.

governance_roi_project_decision_linkage.evaluation_criteria_for_model_quality_or: not reported beyond qualitative claims of traceability, recursion, and generalizability.

roi_value_realization_evidence.details: No cost of adoption, training/tooling effort, saved effort, schedule effect, avoided rework, reuse value metric, decision quality evidence, or mission assurance evidence is reported.

practical_implementation_pathway.rationale: Eight steps are demonstrated with SysML artifacts, although not evaluated in a full project.
evidence: Section 4 Steps 1-8; Figures 1-14.

toolchain_fragmentation_interoperability.rationale: Tool non-dependence is asserted, MagicDraw is shown, and hyperlinks are mentioned, but no fragmentation/interoperability solution is provided.
evidence: Conclusion: 'not dependent on any specific tool'.

lightweight_resource_constrained_tailori.rationale: The method is framed for university CubeSat teams and small, low-cost missions but lacks resource-use evidence or lightweight process metrics.
evidence: Section 3 describes inexpensive/student CubeSat context; Introduction says method for university teams.

governance_project_deliverables_roi.rationale: Single-source model and documentation generation are mentioned, but governance, gates, deliverables, and ROI/value realization are absent.
evidence: Section 2: documentation becomes secondary/generated from model.

newspace_agile_distributed_rapid_iterati.rationale: Rapid growth of CubeSat missions motivates the paper, but no NewSpace/agile/distributed/rapid-iteration process alignment is developed.
evidence: Abstract mentions rapid growth only as background motivation.

RQ1: Provides a clear eight-step SysML workflow for CubeSat behavior modeling from mission requirements through use cases to activity hierarchy/functional architecture.
Useful for general system-level CubeSat modeling and reference-model synthesis; not EPS-specific.
Method assumes well-defined mission requirements and uses generic mission-data collection/distribution examples.
RQ2: Outcome claims include repeatability/generality, traceability, single-source consistency/communication, and generic risk/quality benefits.
No EPS reliability, reproducibility, or integrability outcomes are evidenced; no quantitative outcome evaluation.
RQ3: No verification procedure integration is presented; verification of functional requirements is future work.
No pre-physical EPS/system verification mechanism or V&V artifact is modeled.

author_stated_limitations_or_gaps: Nonfunctional and interface requirements require future work.
Allocation of behaviors to structural elements needs deeper discussion.
Verification of functional requirements is future work.
Only main success scenarios are shown; anomalous scenarios should be considered.
extractor_identified_limitations_or_gaps: No EPS-specific content or power-subsystem evidence.
No quantitative evaluation, baseline, independent validation, reuse across teams, integration/test evidence, or flight evidence.
No model availability/repository or tool interoperability mechanism.
No governance, configuration management, lifecycle gate, or ROI connection.
direct_evidence_quotes_supporting_classi: Abstract: 'This approach provides a repeatable, generalized method for CubeSat development teams to follow...'.
Step 2: 'A refine relationship in SysML is used to reduce ambiguity in a requirement by relating it to another model element that clarifies the requirement.'
Step 6: 'Only the main success scenario is shown in the examples. However, teams should also consider anomalous scenarios as well.'
Conclusion: 'Traceability: There is clear traceability from the mission requirements to the functionality required to satisfy those requirements.'
Future Work: 'The approach presented here just focuses on functional requirements.'
lineage_notes: Treat as CubeSat Reference Model behavior-definition paper within INCOSE SSWG lineage.
Do not count as EPS MBSE or verification-model evidence, despite relevance to general CubeSat system MBSE.
unexpected_observations: Despite early-design method framing, the example preconditions assume an on-orbit, normally operating CubeSat and suitable sensor/orbit capability.
The paper's strongest concrete contribution is artifact structuring/traceability, not evaluated mission performance or reliability improvement.
Tool independence is claimed, but the only implementation shown is MagicDraw and Step 5 explicitly depends on the modeling tool's documentation/hyperlink features.
synthesis_consistency.extraction_confidence_rationale: The paper is method-focused and the markdown captures the relevant sections, figures, appendices, and future work. Confidence is high for what is reported/absent; medium for lifecycle/tailoring classification where phase labels are inferred from requirements/operational scenario context.
